This site is built automatically from the repository's example sources. It is
both documentation for authors and a browser-level regression suite for the
extension.

::: {.callout-note}
All answer checking runs locally in the browser through SymPy and Pyodide.
AI-generated progressive feedback is optional and works with OpenAI-compatible
providers configured by the user.
:::

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Basic features](basic-features.qmd)

Input widths, captions, multiple fields, labels, partial credit, forms, and
random task pools.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [General SymPy examples](sympy-examples.qmd)

Algebra, functions, trigonometry, exact forms, numerical tolerances, sets, and
more involved symbolic answers.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [AI feedback and context](ai-feedback.qmd)

Automatic section context, reusable explicit context, context opt-out,
meaningful field labels, and the model capability adapter.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Vektorer og matriser](vector-matrix-tests.qmd)

En fullstendig norsk testside for rad- og kolonnevektorer, matriser, symbolske
uttrykk, numerisk toleranse og oppgavepooler.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Custom assessment](custom-assessment.qmd)

Five examples of instructor-authored SymPy/Python checkers for properties,
relationships between fields, partial credit, iterative processes, and matrix
constraints.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
### [Graphical assessment](graphics-examples.qmd)

Click-based and draggable JSXGraph responses, movable piecewise-linear graphs,
and freehand polynomial approximations assessed through the generic response
bridge.
:::
:::

## Extended regression page

The original [all-in-one examples page](examples.qmd) remains available. It
contains the large JSXGraph response examples and serves as compatibility
coverage while the focused pages above provide the primary navigation.
